newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Mar pork stocks exagerrated by low '96 level.
newsitem.headline: Japan Mar pork stocks exagerrated by low '96 level.

text.p: Japan's pork stockpiles as of end-March surged 95.8 percent compared with the same period a year earlier, but the rise was exagerrated by exceptionally low stocks during March 1996, industry officials said on Friday.
As of end-March, Japan's pork stocks reached 135,441 tonnes, down by 11.3 percent from end-February but up 95.8 percent from a year earlier, the Agriculture and Livestock Industries Corp said.
Of the total, imported pork stocks rose by 101.5 percent from a year ago to 117,951 tonnes.
During the early months of last year, trade houses were reluctant to import pork because they wanted to wait until the government lifted an emergency tariff on pork in April, industry officials said.
Pork inventories started growing after the government lifted the emergency tariff, they said.
"The Japanese government's tariff policy determines pork imports level here," a pork trader at a major trade house said.
